newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Independent group to monitor Morocco local elections.
newsitem.headline: Independent group to monitor Morocco local elections.

text.p: Morocco's Human Rights Organisation (OMDH) has set up an independent body to monitor local elections due on June 13, the group said on Thursday.
In a statement, the independent OMDH said the watchdog "will monitor the electoral operations and register the violations which might occur during these operations".
The body will later issue a detailed report, the statement said.
More than 102,000 candidates, of which nearly 40,000 belong to the opposition, will compete for 24,253 seats in local council elections.
According to the Interior Ministry, 14,447 candidates are standing as independents. The remainder come from 12 political parties.

Last month, the government announced the creation of a "national commission" to follow up communal and legislative elections. The commission is chaired by supreme court president Driss Dahak and includes the interior and justice ministers and members of a dozen political parties.
Local elections are the first of a series which will be capped by a parliamentary poll in September, with a new bicameral parliament being inaugurated by King Hassan on the second Friday of October.
Under the new constitution, the Lower House of parliament will be directly elected through universal suffrage.
Local councils will elect around 80 percent of the members of new Upper House of Parliament being set up under constitutional reforms approved last September.
The new house will have power to vote a no-confidence motion in the government and could topple it.
